rationale: This is essentially a denominator swap on the archived "Accrual Share of Net Investment" bounded-share construction, and the swap is economically weaker because the signal collapses to ±1 whenever employment growth is near zero (a very common case), so it mostly reproduces the sign of accruals rather than testing the labor-vs-accounting mechanism claimed.

The recch sign convention is handled correctly, capx is nonnegative so the product's direction is unambiguous and matches the stated hypothesis, and isolating the receivable component rather than aggregate accruals is a substantive (not cosmetic) refinement of the archived accrual-loaded capex signal with a clear demand-validation mechanism.

The diagnosis of why the archived level-based inventory interaction had cross-sectional but no portfolio evidence is sensible and the within-firm conditioning is a genuine change, but a 3-period TS_RANK is extremely coarse (effectively three states, with the lowest state annihilating the accrual information entirely), so the construction is noisier and more attenuated than the mechanism warrants.

Replacing leverage level with maturity structure is an economically distinct and defensible conditioning variable, but the scale-free share assigns maximal "refinancing pressure" to firms with trivial total debt that happens to be short-term and is undefined for zero-debt firms, which will inject noise into the extreme portfolio legs.

This is the third instance of the identical archived template "nonnegative balance-sheet share × total accruals" (after inventory/at and dltt/at), differing only in the scaling variable, so it is a cosmetic variant rather than a substantively different mechanism.

Because aqc captures the full cash purchase price while Δgdwl captures only the goodwill portion, the residual is dominated by −aqc, so the signal mechanically assigns *low* values (i.e., predicted high returns) to large cash acquirers — the opposite of the acquisition-underperformance evidence — and additively lumping this with total accruals makes the composite's dominant driver ambiguous.
